newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam renews call for loyalty in armed forces.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam renews call for loyalty in armed forces.

text.p: Vietnam told its armed forces on Wednesday to be loyal to the ruling Communist Party and work to expose hostile forces seeking to undermine Hanoi's leadership.

An editorial in the Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) newspaper said Vietnam's military should carry out political activities aimed at reinforcing support for the Party and "heightening belief in the Party leadership".

"Each cadre, each party member and individual should heighten the spirit of combativity... to fight against the hostile and reactionary points of view and expose the 'peaceful evolution' plots of hostile forces," the daily said.
'Peaceful evolution' is a term used in Vietnam to mean back-door subversion.

Rallying calls for Army-Party unity are common in Vietnam, but there have been few since a major Communist Party congress in late June at which Hanoi elected to extend the terms in office of the country's collective leadership.
In an interview carried in Wednesday's Lao Dong newspaper Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam said some overseas groups might harbour ill will towards Vietnam, but he played down the dangers.
"There are forces which have that intention. But whether they can carry out that intention or not depends on us," he said.
